reports.title: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir (under renovation) and Nursery Pond fishing report
reports.text:
The 70-acre pond has been stocked by the AGFC with mature bass, crappie, catfish and bream (as well as rainbow trout for the cold weather months).
According to AGFC Fisheries staff, there have definitely been times where it is getting a bunch of use and people are catching bream and smaller bass.

reports.title: Harris Brake Lake fishing report
reports.text: As the weather cools, look for bass, bream and catfish to bite, and crappie will become active in a cooler October.

reports.title: Lake Charles fishing report
reports.text:
Marsha Robinson at Lake Charles State Park (870-878-6595) said crappie have made a return, and even a white bass was caught this week, as fishing seemed to pick up across all species other than black bass.
Crappie were fair on jigs and worms, also off the shoreline.

reports.title: Lake Hamilton fishing report
reports.text: As usual we are seeing small pods of bass chasing shad and catching them casting spoons, swimbaits and trolling For the crappie fishermen, the crappie are in fall transition with the water starting to cool. Deeper brushpiles near the channels at the entrance of coves and smaller creek arms are holding some nice crappie.

reports.title: Lake Maumelle fishing report
reports.text: “We are seeing bass schooling,” they report. “Caught a few small crappie this week.”

reports.title: Little Maumelle River fishing report
reports.text:
Ray Hudson at River Valley Marina (501-517-1250) said the water is normal clear, and there have been some very active crappie and a few catches.
Fish a cork and a jig in 6 feet of water and expect to find those crappie at 3 feet.
“ Bass are still doing really good.

reports.title: Peckerwood Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Donna Mulherin at Herman’s Landing (501-626-6899) said in her most recent report that lingering summer heat was not deterring the crappie anglers. Conditions have been just right – low water, stumps showing and the main channel obvious – to put crappie fishermen in close proximity to their quest. “They are wearing the crappie out.
Jigs are the bait of choice at Peckerwood for crappie.
Those good conditions for crappie are a nonstarter for bass, though, and while a few people have picked up some catfish, the chief draw now is crappie. “You can’t do much else” than crappie fish, Donna says.

reports.title: Arkansas’ Lake Ouachita: Where Smart Crappie Fishing Pays Off
reports.text:
Oklahoma crappie pro Todd Huckabee used a detailed game plan to help him
find Lake Ouachita’s clear-water slabs the first time he fished this huge impoundment.
Arkansas’ Lake Ouachita: Where Smart Crappie Fishing Pays Off
Story and photos by Keith Sutton
Some crappie lakes give up their secrets easily. Lake Ouachita isn’t one of them.
That’s not to say the fishing is poor. Quite the opposite. Arkansas’ largest lake has an excellent population of black and white crappie, and anglers who understand how to find them can enjoy some mighty fine fishing. reports.title: Brewer Lake fishing report
reports.text: Brewer Lake is a good getaway in the fall for crappie fishing as well as picking up some decent-sized largemouth bass. For crappie, focus on coves in the northern portion of the lake. Bass in coming weeks should be found on secondary points and isolated brush. Anglers may keep up to 10 largemouths, but only one of those may exceed 16 inches.
